hero: Use case: stylized-concept. Create a polished landscape pixel-art character design sheet for the original student 2D side-scrolling roguelite MARÉ BAIXA. This is visual development, not a finished sprite atlas. Deep midnight teal background, warm cream small clean labels, tasteful professional game art direction. Title "MARÉ BAIXA" and subtitle "CASCO · ESTUDO DE PERSONAGEM". Six equally prominent full-body designs, in a spacious 3 by 2 layout. Consistent original young orange hermit crab Casco in each cell, facing right in lateral three-quarter view suitable for a platformer: two big expressive stalk eyes, oversized claws, small crab legs, soft curled exposed abdomen when without shell, curious brave slightly clumsy expression. Same anatomy, same scale, orange body in every variant. Each design clearly separated. Row one: label "SEM CONCHA" shell-less vulnerable Casco; "CONCHA COMUM" Casco wearing a simple sandy rounded shell; "TAMPINHA" Casco wearing a small teal corrugated metal bottle cap as armor. Row two: "CONCHA ESPIRAL" Casco wearing a distinct spiral cream sea shell; "LATA" Casco wearing a dented unbranded green soda can with visible aluminum rim as a bulky shelter; "LÂMPADA" Casco wearing an old translucent warm glowing lightbulb shelter with screw base visible, his orange body outside the bulb. Pixel art with deliberate large square pixels, limited palette, 1-pixel dark navy outlines at logical sprite scale, 2-3 shades per material, clearly readable silhouette inspired by constraints of 32x32 game art but enlarged for concept readability. Do not pretend the sheet is a technically exact 32x32 atlas. No smooth painting, no 3D, no human limbs, no weapons, no brand marks, no decorative scenery, no additional characters. Small restrained palette swatches at bottom. Friendly fantasy action appropriate ages 10+. Preserve clear distinction of all five shells.
npc: Use case: stylized-concept. Original game MARÉ BAIXA, 2D side-view pixel art visual development sheet for four friendly marine NPCs. Landscape 3:2 canvas, spacious 2x2 grid on solid midnight teal background, cream typography. Title "MARÉ BAIXA" subtitle "MORADORES DA VILA". Chunky deliberate square pixel clusters, dark navy contour, 2-3 clear shade steps per material, orange/coral/sand/turquoise palette, charming readable silhouettes for a pixel art platform game. Four full body separate character concepts, not an exact sprite atlas. Upper left label "VOVÓ BÚZIA": elderly hermit crab, muted burnt orange small body, enormous elongated sandy whelk shell towering diagonally behind her, kind eye stalks, slightly stooped, tiny driftwood walking stick in claw, no human body. Upper right label "OSTRÁCIA": anthropomorphic oyster merchant, wide open scalloped lavender-gray oyster shell on seabed, expressive face inside pearly mantle, admiring small pearls displayed at her base, distinct fan silhouette, no human body. Lower left label "DONA LAGOSTA": coral red lobster blacksmith, clearly lobster with long segmented tail and antennae, large claws, dark small work apron and modest salvage hammer, grumpy talented expression, sturdy upright crablike stance, no human legs or hands. Lower right label "BOLOTA": baby pufferfish, small round golden sandy body with cream belly, tiny fins and soft short spines, huge worried eyes, timid adorable comic companion. Keep friendly Bolota clearly distinguishable from hostile pufferfish: small soft spines, rounded brow, fearful expression. Each creature fills its quadrant with generous safe margins, no overlap. Cohesive original designs, not copies of existing games. No landscape or UI, no extra characters, no weapons except blacksmith tool, no blood, no smooth illustration, no 3D. Restrained palette swatches at bottom. Characters are concept art intended to be simplified into 32x32 and 48x48 sprites.
